title: Certify only what passes every re-grade
statement: Certify a generated item only if it passes every identical re-grading, treating a flip as a sign of a real defect.
example: Items flipping at scores of 0.80 to 0.85 were real defects, and items at 0.95 or above held.
detail: A review of a proposed item factory found that every lens endorsed its flip-band, stably-pass gate: items that flipped at 0.80-0.85 were real defects and items at 0.95 or above held (`grade3-reading/artifacts/GOAL_grade3_hootl_convergence_2026_06_15.md`). The same record warns that the gate filters score noise, not score bias, so a confidently mis-graded item certifies forever. A review of eight course proposals kept flip-band, stably-pass certification as part of the one proposal that manufactures and re-certifies item banks (`grade3-reading/artifacts/PROPOSAL_REVIEW_2026_06_16.md`).
against: The evidence came from AP history items (`grade3-reading/artifacts/PROPOSAL_REVIEW_2026_06_16.md`), and a tightly specified AI marker in a reading lesson did not flip at all, identical in 12 of 12 scenario runs (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-16-R24.md`).

evidence.quote: The flip-band stably-pass gate is load-bearing hygiene every lens endorsed (0.80-0.85 flips are real defects, >=0.95 holds) but it filters score NOISE, not score BIAS
